meta.purpose: Country-level risk INPUT for Lexo's compliance engine. Scores are Lexo's internal points, not scores issued by FATF, the EU or OFAC.
usageRules: Country risk is one input among several. It must never be the sole basis for rejecting a person.
Nationality or residence is not evidence of criminal activity.
Country-level lists are separate from person/wallet sanctions screening (e.g. SDN matches); do not merge them.
Countries not in this file have no elevated indicator in the three selected sources (score 0, LOW by default). That is an absence of listing, not a finding of low risk.

scoring.doubleCounting: EU points are reduced to 2 when FATF already lists the country (EU list is FATF-based); EU-only listings get 6. OFAC points are additive because OFAC sanctions are a separate, non-AML basis.

conflicts.detail: Still on the EU list (in force 2025-08-05) but FATF's 2026-06-19 statement says both are no longer under increased monitoring. Likely EU update lag; scored on the EU listing only (6 pts, independent rule) and flagged.
Listed by the EU (2016/2018 entries) but not on either FATF list in June 2026. Scored as EU-independent designations.
Listed by the EU since 2026-01-29 (category for suspended FATF members); FATF lists neither call-for-action nor increased-monitoring for Russia (membership suspended since 2023-02-24).

On FATF increased monitoring (Kuwait and PNG since Feb 2026; Bosnia and Herzegovina and Iraq since Jun 2026) but absent from the EU list, whose latest amendment on the EC page is dated 2026-01-09. Probably timing; no EU update after that date was found (see unverified items).
On FATF grey list; the EU high-risk list covers third countries only and Bulgaria is an EU member state.

OFAC ended comprehensive sanctions (effective 2025-07-01; state-sponsor designation rescinded 2026-08-24) and keeps only list-based PAARSS, while FATF and the EU still list Syria (FATF text is from Feb 2023). Several secondary sources still describe Syria as comprehensively sanctioned; OFAC's own page contradicts them.

OFAC's blocking of the Government of Venezuela remains in the legal framework but is heavily eased by general licenses through Sep 2026, while FATF and the EU list Venezuela. Scored on program structure, not on license activity.

FATF calls for EDD (not countermeasures) on Myanmar and will consider countermeasures if no progress by Oct 2026; the EU lists Myanmar; OFAC's Burma program treated as targeted. Consistent direction, different intensity.
FATF still lists these but has made an initial determination that the action plan is substantially complete; removal depends on an on-site assessment. Score not reduced until FATF delists.

unverified: EU list currency: the EC page was last updated 2026-01-09 (list in force from 2026-01-29). No later delegated regulation was found in searches, but this could not be confirmed on an official EC page dated after that.

OFAC: only the program index, the 'no country list' page, and the PAARSS, Venezuela and Ukraine-/Russia-related pages were read in full. For all other programs the index entry (name and last-updated date) is the evidence; tier assignments for them are Lexo judgments, not OFAC statements.
OFAC North Korea: 'comprehensive' tier not confirmed on an OFAC page (secondary sources only). OFAC Cuba and Iran: confirmed as broad-based/geographic on OFAC's country-list page.

OFAC Russia: tier 'broad' not confirmed on the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities program page itself. OFAC Belarus and Burma: tier set to 'targeted' without reading the program pages; manual review recommended.
OFAC Balkans-Related Sanctions: program exists, but which countries it covers was not verified, so Bosnia and Herzegovina (or any other Balkan state) receives no OFAC points.

Ukraine: the Ukraine-/Russia-related program targets regions (Crimea etc. appear in the E.O. list, e.g. E.O. 13685) and persons, not Ukraine as a country. Ukraine is NOT scored; sub-national regions have no ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, so none are included.
Global/thematic OFAC programs (counter terrorism, counter narcotics, cyber, Global Magnitsky, TCO, non-proliferation, CAATSA, ICC, etc.) are not country programs and were not used for country scores.
FATF texts for Syria and Yemen are dated Feb 2023, and for Kuwait and Papua New Guinea Feb 2026 (they deferred reporting); FATF says these may not reflect current status.
EU 'Russia is in a separate category' detail comes from the Malta FIAU summary of Reg. 2026/46; the EC page itself lists Russia in its table without that explanation.
Absence of a listing is not evidence of low risk: FATF notes some jurisdictions have not yet been reviewed. Nothing here covers UN, UK, or national sanctions lists.
